title: Loops (while)
concept: The while loop repeats as long as the condition is true. It's ideal when the number of iterations isn't predetermined.

steps.title: Starting the main Function
steps.explanation:
The main stack frame is created when the program starts.

This lesson focuses on understanding how a while loop progresses and terminates through condition checks and value updates.

steps.title: Setting the Initial Value
steps.explanation:
`int n = 1;` prepares the variable for the while loop outside the loop body.

Since while requires you to manually write initialization and updates, it's important to clearly set the starting value.

steps.title: while Condition Check (n = 1)
steps.explanation:
First checks whether `n <= 4` is true, then executes the body if it is.

Since while is a condition-driven loop, forgetting to update the condition variable easily leads to an infinite loop.

steps.title: Iteration 1: Print Current Value
steps.explanation:
Prints the current value of `n` to track the loop's progress.

In while loops, these intermediate outputs are useful for debugging the flow.

steps.title: Iteration 1: Double n
steps.explanation:
`n = n * 2;` changes n from 1 to 2. In a while loop, this kind of update code is essential.

Without the update, the condition stays true forever and creates an infinite loop.

steps.title: Iteration 2: Condition Check (n = 2)
steps.explanation:
After the update, `n=2` so the condition is still true and the next iteration proceeds.

The flow repeats: `condition check -> execute body -> update value`.

steps.title: Iteration 3: Condition Check (n = 4)
steps.explanation:
At `n=4`, `n <= 4` is still true so the body executes one more time.

After this update, n becomes 8, which will terminate the loop at the next check.

steps.title: Loop Terminates (n = 8)
steps.explanation:
When `n=8`, `8 <= 4` is false so the while loop exits.

Note that upon loop exit, the variable's value may not be the "last executed value" but rather the "value that broke the condition".

steps.title: Printing Final n
steps.explanation:
Prints the final value of `n` after the loop ends.

This confirms that the exit value isn't the last printed value, but rather the value after the condition was broken.

steps.title: Program Exit
steps.explanation:
`return 0;` terminates the program normally.

The key takeaway from this example is that in a while loop, you must manage the condition and update yourself.

quiz.question: How does while (1) { ... } behave?
quiz.explanation:
In C, 1 is true and 0 is false.

`while (1)` means the condition is always true, so it loops infinitely.
You need a `break` statement to exit.

misconceptions.wrong: A while loop executes at least once even if the condition is false
misconceptions.correct: If the condition is false from the start, while never executes.
misconceptions.why:
The loop that guarantees at least one execution is do-while.
while checks the condition before entering the body.

keyTakeaway: The while loop is for 'when you don't know when it will end' — it keeps repeating as long as the condition is true!
